current_price.unit: per bushel (CBOT ZW Sep'26 at 640.25¢ post-roll)

thesis_summary: Global wheat is in a genuine ~4 MMT supply deficit for MY 2026/27 with major-exporter stocks-to-use near 8% and a developing strong El Niño threatening a second consecutive tightening year, but the current 632¢/bu price already embeds an estimated $0.50-0.80/bu Black Sea war-risk premium that is binary and reversible; the highest-information data window (USDA WASDE August 12, NOAA ENSO August 13) is 31 days away, making initiation today a decision to pay now for evidence available in one month.
key_risks: Black Sea war-risk premium dissolves on ceasefire or maritime corridor deal — price retraces ~8-13% to the estimated $5.50-5.80/bu fundamental floor
Russia's 88 MMT crop exports fully at zero duty, capping CBOT upside and removing the key supply-offset uncertainty
India expands wheat export quota beyond the current 5 MMT cap, adding non-Russian supply
El Niño weakens unexpectedly — NOAA August update lowers very-strong-event probability, removing the second-season tightening narrative
Contango roll drag of ~8-9%/yr structurally penalises any ETF (WEAT) long position that fails to outrun the carry cost

key_levels.fair_value_range: 550-580 (fundamental-only, stripping war-risk premium per macro-positioning synthesis)

relative_view: WHEAT has a real supply deficit and historically tight exporter buffer but is not the best-positioned commodity in the tracked universe today — its bull case is hostage to a binary geopolitical premium, the curve drag (~9%/yr) is structurally punitive, and the August 12 WASDE is the cleanest entry signal 31 days away; corn (near-term pollination weather catalyst) and gold (macro-conditional, lower carry cost) offer cleaner setups in the current window
